releaseNotes: Split "actively operating the business" into separately-gated lanes. Support-queue operation, retention intervention, and the financial health review were prose bullets inside the single Weekly Ops Review node — an autonomous run had no distinct obligation to prove a ticket was answered, a churn cohort was worked, or the money was read. Each is now its own weekly-recurring catalog node with its own artifact (operations/SUPPORT_OPS.md, RETENTION_OPS.md, FINANCE_OPS.md) and its own fail-closed section in check:post-launch: counted queue state and a stated SLA, a named cohort source with measured D7/D30 values and an intervention log, and an MRR-labeled dollar figure with spend and runway — placeholders, adjectives, and stale rows all fail once the app has been live past two weeks, and a recorded Kill verdict remains the one legitimate quiet.

The Weekly Ops Review now READS the three lane artifacts, which makes the cycle self-ordering: recurrence reopens all four nodes each week, the lane nodes re-produce first, and their changed outputs invalidate the review so it re-runs over fresh numbers — no hand-authored ordering. role.customer-success owns its first operating nodes (support, retention — its charter always said response queues and churn routing), with its write scope widened to exactly those two artifacts.
Eleven fail-then-catch fixture cases plus a green control past the stand-up window join the lifecycle suite; the real-catalog count assertion moves 93 -> 96.
